physical.notes: The vendor gives the product size as 56.0 x 40.0 x 16.0 mm; width and height here are the front face upright, as the drawings use them. Package 80.0 x 45.0 x 20.0 mm, gross weight 42.6 g. Enclosure: plastic (PC). Operating temperature 0 to 60 C. Magnetic back.

specs.cpu: Xtensa 32-bit LX6, dual core, up to 240 MHz
specs.chip_revision: v1.0 or v1.1 (the datasheet's ordering table; which one a given unit carries is not stated by the vendor)
specs.lifecycle: Not recommended for new designs (NRND), per the datasheet
specs.supply_net: MCU_VDD on VDDA (1, 43, 46), VDDA3P3 (3, 4), VDD3P3_RTC (19) and VDD3P3_CPU (37); decoupling C46 22 uF, C10, C12 to C15 and C18 1 uF. VDD_SDIO (26) is an output of the module (fed inside from VDD3P3_RTC while MTDI is low at reset), with only C16 1 uF to GND
specs.in_package_flash_pins: IO6/CLK FLASH_CLK, IO16 FLASH_CS, IO8/SD1 SI/SIO0, IO17 SO/SIO1, IO7/SD0 WP/SIO2, IO11/CMD HOLD/SIO3 (datasheet Table 3); not for other use

pins.LNA_IN (pin 2): ANT1 through a pi network: C4 1.5 pF to GND, L1 1.8 nH in series, C6 1.2 pF to GND

components.notes: Every GPIO the board uses is listed on the peripheral it reaches. GPIO numbers are the U1 pin names; the schematic's U1 pin numbers are given where a pin is unused.

specs.interface: SPI; BS1 tied to GND on the board, which selects 4-wire 8-bit SPI

connects_to.bus: SPI; no separate MISO line reaches the panel connector: the panel answers register and RAM reads on SDA (GPIO23), half-duplex three-wire
connects_to.notes: GPIO0 is also the ESP32 boot strap the USB-UART auto-reset drives (usb-uart). The reads over SDA are what the Kleidos firmware does on this board (EpaperPanelDriver::makePanelReadDevice and EpaperPanelDriver::readPanelRegister in src/hal/display/epaper_panel_driver.cpp), with which it read the controller's identity back.

pins.RESE (3): Q6 source, current sense across R47 0.47 ohm (net EPD_IS)

components.notes: Pin names and numbers as the vendor schematic's EPD1 symbol writes them; the symbol is named EPD_SPI and names no panel model. Each of VGL (4), VGH (5), VDD (18), VPP (19), VSH (20), VSL (22) and VCOM (24) has a 1 uF/25 V capacitor to GND (C35 to C41); BSI (8), VSS (17) and the shell go to GND. The GDEY0154D67 specification names pin 4 NC and pin 5 VSH2. M5Stack states for this panel: viewing area 27.0 x 27.0 mm, dot pitch 0.14 mm, 184 DPI, refresh 2 s, partial refresh 0.26 s, 'grayscale: 2'; Good Display's product page states 4 gray levels. M5Stack changed the panel from GDEW0154M09 to GDEY0154D67 on 2024-10-25. On one unit the Kleidos firmware read the controller's identity back as SSD1681.

specs.mounting: chip on glass inside the GDEY0154D67 panel module

connects_to.notes: The controller is inside the panel module; its signals are the panel connector's pins.

components.notes: Good Display's GDEY0154D67 specification names the SSD1681 as the panel's driver, and on one unit the Kleidos firmware read the controller's identity back as SSD1681.

specs.function: switch of the panel's gate-voltage booster, driven by the SSD1681's GDR pin
specs.circuit: MCU_VDD -> L4 10 uH -> Q6 drain; Q6 source -> R47 0.47 ohm -> GND; C34 10 uF/6.3 V on the input
specs.vgg_output: D15 1N5819 from the switch node to VGG, C45 1 uF/25 V
specs.vee_output: C43 1 uF/25 V from the switch node into a D16/D17 1N5819 charge pump to VEE, C44 1 uF/25 V

specs.type: synchronous boost, output disconnected in shutdown
specs.input_net: BST_IN (SYS_BAT through D10 SS34, or CHG through D9 1N5819)
specs.feedback: R43 15 kohm from OUT to FB, R44 4.7 kohm from FB to GND

pins.EN (3): PS_EN, Q4's drain through R50 10 kohm

components.notes: vout_v_computed is VOUT = 1.2 V x (RH/RL + 1) from the datasheet with the schematic's 15 kohm and 4.7 kohm. SYS_P050 feeds the 3.3 V buck and, through D11 1N5819, EXT_5VO (C29 10 uF), the 5 V of the Grove port, the M5-Bus 5VOUT, the HAT connector and the buzzer.

specs.feedback: R39 22 kohm from the output to FB, R40 5.1 kohm from FB to GND

components.notes: The schematic gives no suffix for the part, and its datasheet was not read for this file, so the output voltage is stated only by the schematic's section title. MCU_VDD supplies the ESP32-PICO-D4, the panel logic, the ESD arrays, the pull-ups, the M5-Bus 3V3 and the HAT connector.

specs.prog: R45 5.1 kohm from PROG (pin 6) to GND
specs.chg_pin: CHG# (pin 1) sinks LED1 through R34 2.2 kohm from CHG

components.notes: The schematic writes the part as 'TP40P57'; the vendor's block diagram, the second image of the docs page's schematic section, names it TP4057. No datasheet has been read against the schematic's pin names yet, so no maker is given here, and the charge current PROG sets is not computed.

specs.function: battery power switch: source on SYS_BAT, drain on the switched battery that enables the 5 V boost (PS_EN) and feeds the battery ADC divider
specs.gate: R32 100 kohm to SYS_BAT (off by default); PWR_TRIG through R36 47 ohm (pulled low to switch on)

pins.drain (switched battery): GPIO35 through a divider, R41 20 kohm over R42 5.1 kohm, C30 1 uF/6.3 V to GND

components.notes: PWR_TRIG is pulled low by any of: Q5 (held by GPIO12 or by USB 5 V), the power button (through D6), or the RTC's INT# (through D13).

specs.function: power hold: drain on PWR_TRIG, source on GND; while on it keeps the Q4 battery switch on

connects_to.notes: The vendor calls GPIO12 HOLD: driven high it keeps the board powered.

pins.gate: USB_5V through D19 4148 and R51 5.1 kohm

connects_to.notes: With USB 5 V present the latch is held on whatever GPIO12 does.

specs.supply_net: SYS_BAT, the battery ahead of the power switch (C25 100 nF/10 V)

connects_to.notes: GPIO21 and GPIO22 also reach the M5-Bus (pins 9 and 10) through 47 ohm resistors.
An RTC alarm or timer pulling INT# low pulls PWR_TRIG low and switches the board on.

specs.supply: VBUS (8) and REGIN (7) on USB_5V (C3 10 uF/6.3 V); VIO (5) tied to VDD (6), the on-chip regulator's output (C5 100 nF/10 V)

pins.DTR (23), RTS (19): EN and GPIO0 through the Q2/Q3 S8050 auto-reset pair

connects_to.notes: Auto-reset: Q2 has its base on DTR through R30 10 kohm, its emitter on RTS and its collector on EN; Q3 has its base on RTS through R31 10 kohm, its emitter on DTR and its collector on GPIO0 through D7 4148 (cathode on Q3). EN also has C17 1 uF to GND.

components.notes: The vendor's documentation says the board ships in two versions, one with a CP2104 and one with a CH9102 USB-UART chip; the schematic shows the CP2104 version.
They sit on the ESP32 side of the 47 ohm series resistors (R6 to R16) that lead the same lines to the M5-Bus. The Grove port's G32 and G33 have their series resistors but no ESD array.

uses.D8: USB_5V into the charger input (towards FU1 and CHG)

specs.use: SYS_BAT into BST_IN, the boost's input

uses.D14: GPIO12 to the power latch's gate
uses.D18: base clamp of the buzzer driver Q1
uses.D19: USB_5V to the power latch's gate

specs.position: between the 5 V input (USB_5V after D8, joined by EXT_5VI) and CHG, the charger input

specs.drive: from CHG through R34 2.2 kohm, sunk by the charger's CHG# pin; not on a GPIO
GPIO10, lit when the pin is low
specs.location: inside the case, near the top

connects_to.notes: J1 pin 1 is GPIO10, with no series part on the main board; the LED and its resistor are beyond J1, off the schematic.

components.notes: The vendor's pin map gives G10 as the LED. The vendor's specification table lists one green LED. On the owner's unit it is green, sits inside the case near the top, and lit on the Kleidos firmware's LED-on command (owner observed on his unit, 2026-11-17). That command drives GPIO10 to the level the firmware declares as on, which is low (STATUS_LED_ACTIVE_LOW in the Kleidos firmware's variants/m5core_ink/variant.h, taken as the off level's inverse by statusLedOffLevel in src/hal/common/peripheral_switch.cpp; the pin driven as a plain push-pull output, schematic/bench/2026-11-17-led-and-user-key.md), so the LED is lit when GPIO10 is low.

specs.supply: EXT_5VO through R5 4.7 ohm to BZ1 +
specs.driver: Q1 S8050 low side on BZ1 -, D4 4148 flyback across BZ1
specs.drive_path: GPIO2 -> R2 2.2 kohm -> C1 10 uF/6.3 V (AC coupling) -> Q1 base; D18 4148 clamps the base to GND

specs.type: three-way dial switch: roll up, press, roll down
specs.common: C to GND, so each position reads low when active

connects_to.notes: Each line also has 1 uF/6.3 V to GND: C9 on GPIO37, C7 on GPIO38, C8 on GPIO39.

specs.type: side push button to GND (the schematic's value is a Chinese description of a side-press key)
specs.use: press and hold to power on
specs.location: right side as the front is seen, the dial's side, under the dial

connects_to.notes: GPIO27 also has C2 1 uF/6.3 V to GND.
A press pulls PWR_TRIG low and switches Q4 on.

components.notes: A push key, not a slide switch, on the same side as the dial (owner observed on his unit, 2026-11-17). The back sticker points at it with 'Switch G27' and 'POWER ON'.

specs.type: push button to GND on MCU_RST (ESP32 EN)
specs.use: reset; the vendor gives it as the way to power off
specs.location: on the back, beside the sticker's SYSTEM RST arrow

components.notes: On the back of the case (owner observed on his unit, 2026-11-17); svg/back.svg draws it.

connects_to.notes: J1 pin 2 is GPIO5, with no pull-up on the main board; the button and any pull-up are beyond J1, off the schematic.

components.notes: The vendor's pin map gives G5 as the User Button. On the top end of the case (owner observed on his unit, 2026-11-17).

specs.matching: pi network: C4 1.5 pF to GND, L1 1.8 nH in series, C6 1.2 pF to GND

specs.net: the same antenna feed as ANT1, after the pi network

components.notes: The schematic draws ANT1 and ANT2 on one feed; it does not say whether both are fitted.

specs.vbus_net: USB_5V (to the CP2104, to the charger input through D8 1N5819 and FU1, and to the power latch through D19)
specs.data: DP1/DP2 joined and DN1/DN2 joined, each through a 47 ohm resistor (R17, R18)

pinout.3: 5VIN (EXT_5VI, joins the 5 V input after D8)

connects_to.notes: Each signal passes a 47 ohm series resistor (R6 to R16) with an SRV05-4 ESD array on the ESP32 side.

components.notes: The vendor's pin breakout list is G25, G26, G36, G23, G34, G18, G21, G22, G14, G13.

specs.type: 10-pin FPC, 'FPC TO HAT': links the main board to the top HAT expansion interface

connects_to.notes: The top HAT expansion interface the vendor lists.

absent.notes: The ESP32-PICO-D4 has no in-package PSRAM and the board fits none.
Power is discrete: a charger, a boost, a buck and a MOSFET switch.
The battery is read through a resistor divider on GPIO35.
The buzzer is driven by one transistor.
The board's one sound part is a passive buzzer.

notes: The connections come from the vendor's one-page schematic, which carries no revision or date. The LED on GPIO10 and the button on GPIO5 sit beyond the 'FPC TO HAT' connector J1 and are not drawn on it. Net names in specs (SYS_BAT, SYS_P050, MCU_VDD, EXT_5VO, EXT_5VI, CHG, BST_IN, PWR_TRIG, PS_EN) are the schematic's. The vendor powers the board on with a long press of the side power button and off with the reset button or software.
